note: SCOPE_1.8.7 §6.3 / OPERATOR_BROADCAST.md — the Class D wire contract. Three implementations have to agree: the admin endpoint that writes it, and two clients that read it. A client that silently drops a valid broadcast is an outage nobody hears about; a client that renders an invalid one is an unvalidated string from the network on a HIGH-importance channel.

tags.note: A newer version fixes something the user is living with. The only tag that may carry applies_to_versions_at_or_below.
A service the app depends on is degraded or down, with an expected shape to it.
A defect in the running build that the user needs to know about now.

_tag_note: Closed vocabulary, enforced on the endpoint AND on both clients. There is no OTHER, no free-form category and no way to add one from the admin UI, because 'nothing promotional' has to be a property of the system rather than a rule someone remembers at 11pm on a slow month.

invalid.note: The single most important rejection in the file. A client that passes an unknown tag through is a client that will render whatever the next person types into the category box.
A title longer than the shade shows is a title whose end nobody reads. Truncating silently would let an operator believe they said something they did not.
Plaintext is refused rather than upgraded. A link arriving over the network and opened from a HIGH-importance notification is not the place to be permissive.

Version filtering exists so an update notice is true for the device that gets it. On any other tag it is a segmentation lever with no operational meaning, so the shape forbids it rather than trusting nobody to reach for it.
